sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Pharmacological studies performed on the FLAG-tagged GALR1 construct (L1), implying ligand-binding function preserved; HiBiT-GALR1 (L4/L5) showed specific tracer displacement by galanin in NanoBRET target engagement assay, confirming functional galanin binding at the surface-displayed receptor.
sites.rationale: GALR1 has no endogenous signal peptide; residues 1–33 are extracellular per the authoritative topology landmarks, making the N-terminus the only extracellular terminus available for tagging. The FLAG construct (L1) uses an exogenous HA signal to drive the receptor to the membrane with FLAG displayed extracellularly before residue 1 (M), placing the tag at insert_after_residue=0. No residue number is named in either L1 or L4/L5, so position is topology-derived: with a single extracellular terminus and a prepend architecture, only one junction exists. The TM1 boundary begins at residue 34, leaving 33 residues of extracellular space—well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum—and the pharmacological and NanoBRET data confirm both surface display and functional galanin engagement. Human GALR1 cloned into pcDNA3.1(+) with an exogenous N-terminal HA signal sequence followed by a FLAG epitope tag (DYKDDDDK), creating a full-length membrane-anchored receptor construct used for structural and pharmacological studies. Corroborated by L4/L5: HiBiT-GALR1 (same N-terminal prepend architecture) expressed on the surface of living HeLa cells, with surface display confirmed by filtered bioluminescence imaging and receptor engagement validated by NanoBRET with galanin competition.

sources.claim: The human GALR1 and GALR2 were cloned into pcDNA3.1(+) vector (Thermo Fisher Scientific) with an N-terminal hemagglutinin (HA) signal sequence and a FLAG epitope tag (DYKDDDDK).

literature_notes: L1 and L4/L5 both support the identical N-terminal prepend junction (insert_after_residue=0) with different tags (FLAG and HiBiT respectively); these are reported as one site since the junction is the same. No residue number is named in either paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived: GALR1 has no signal peptide, residues 1–33 are extracellular, and the prepend architecture leaves exactly one possible extracellular junction. L2/L3 (C-terminal mCherry knock-in) is placed in other_positions because the C-terminus (residues 307–349) is intracellular per the authoritative topology. No ledger line supports an insertion in ECL1 (94–109), ECL2 (173–198), or ECL3 (269–285), so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal mCherry knock-in at the 3′ end of the GalR1 coding sequence; the C-terminus (residues 307–349) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
